items.reason: Pinning a tag to a commit SHA means asking GitHub what the tag points at right now, and this session has no network; the repo already has the one-command close (`npm run actions:pin`, which also flips STRICT and the P6 ratchet in the same pass), and every workflow's permissions are already job-scoped least privilege, so there was nothing left to do offline.

Already covered another way: .github/branch-ruleset.json declares the ruleset, scripts/branch-protection.mjs reconciles it against .github/required-checks.json offline and blocks through `npm run merge-gate` inside check:ci, and `npm run protection:verify` reads GitHub's live rules weekly in agent-review-history.yml and publishes the answer into the trail issue.

Added a lessons ledger keyed by the mistake — nine traps with evidence, the correct call and whether anything now stops them — routed from AGENTS.md and the task index, held to the tree by a blocking unit test and given an age budget so it is re-read when the guidance moves.

Added a performance budget: five key-free routes with declared ceilings, measured as the warm document response (best of three) by a Playwright spec in the required E2E job, with the registry's shape held by a blocking unit test.

Already covered another way: test-llm/model-pins.json records which model surface every golden, bake and budget was accepted against, `llm:models:check` and test-unit/llm-model-pin.test.mjs block when src/lib/llm/models.ts declares a model the pins do not, llm-drift.yml re-proves the whole registry against the configured provider weekly, and test-llm/model-candidates.json rehearses the successor before a swap.

Progressive delivery is a platform and release decision, not a repo file: the deploy target is already declared as data (.github/environments.json, diffed against the tree on every build), and staged exposure on Vercel plus any rollout gate would change how a push reaches users — which AGENTS.md puts squarely on the operator, and which no test here could hold.

The provenance mechanism is already complete (scripts/commit-attribution.mjs writes Agent-Harness/Model/Spec/Session/Lane, install-commit-hooks.mjs wires it on `npm install`, commit:check reports coverage); the one repo-side lever left was committing the two managed hooks so worktree lanes inherit them without an install, and this session was refused write access to .husky/ — a maintainer should decide whether to track them, given the installer deliberately never overwrites a human-owned hook.

lessons: This repository's convention is that every new fence arrives as a trio — the declaration as data in .github/, the thing that measures it, and a census test that fails when the declaration stops describing the tree. Matching that shape matters more than the fence itself: test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs refuses a check:ci stage with no rule attached, so a gate added without its row turns the suite red.

Rung discipline (ADR-0007) is the load-bearing idea here: a check blocks only once somebody has measured that it passes. An offline session cannot measure, so anything it adds should either block on SHAPE (which is checkable from committed data) or ship with a null baseline and the command that pins it — never with an invented threshold.
An isolated worktree session may be denied writes to hook directories like .husky/, so plans that depend on committing a git hook need a human step; check that before designing a fix around one.
